hypothesis: The note's section 9.7 asks for posterior sampling; the missing-data case was 'cheap, not asked'. A missing site is a site with no likelihood, and forward-filter backward-sample returns whole posterior sequences, so an exact-BP denoiser gives calibrated uncertainty inside a gap, where a Gaussian conditional cannot (a gap in a bimodal field spans a kink). E45 asks what E33's frozen fitted kernels do when part of a noisy sequence is hidden.
design: No refit and no cluster. Kernels: E33's FROZEN fits at M = 2048 (risk-selected checkpoints, seeds 0-15) for em_pair_quartic (hpc_E33q), em_tilted_spline and em_mixture (hpc_E33k), rebuilt from the theta column by e34_field_physics.kernel_from_row; plus the oracle (the true kernel) and the linear Gaussian conditional with the TRUE covariance (the Kalman smoother with missing data). Cells T0.3_h1_L32 and T1_iso_L32; 256 fresh exact sequences per (cell, seed), noised at t = 0.5; hidden patterns random50 (16 of 32 sites, a fixed random subset per seed), gap8 (sites 12-19) and gap16 (sites 8-23); a hidden site has variance 1e8 (flat likelihood; verified: changing a hidden observation changes the posterior by exactly 0). Posterior mean by grid BP; 200 FFBS samples with jitter; per (cell, seed, arm, pattern) the relative squared error at the hidden sites and the coverage and mean width of the 90% central interval (linear: mean +- 1.645 sd). Laptop.

predeclared_predictions.P1: The machinery is calibrated: the oracle's 90% intervals cover the truth with frequency in [0.87, 0.93] on every (cell, pattern), pooled over seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P2: The learned site energy keeps it: its coverage is within 0.03 of 0.90 on every (cell, pattern) pooled over seeds, and its hidden-site error is within 10% of the oracle's in at least 14 of 16 seeds on every (cell, pattern).
predeclared_predictions.P3: The linear conditional is miscalibrated where a gap spans a kink: |coverage - 0.90| > 0.03 on (T0.3_h1_L32, gap16), pooled over seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P4: The posterior MEAN is not where the nonlinear model wins: on (T0.3_h1_L32, gap16) the ratio of the linear to the oracle hidden-site error (seed means) is in [0.9, 1.1].
predeclared_predictions.P5: The UNCERTAINTY is: on (T0.3_h1_L32, gap16) the linear 90% interval is at least 10% wider than the oracle's (ratio of seed-mean widths >= 1.1).

predeclared_analysis: inpainting.csv: per (cell, pattern, arm) pooled coverage and mean width over seeds; hidden-site error ratios per seed and of seed means; a failed rebuild (a failed E33 fit) counts against every clause it touches; read by tools/make_extension_numbers.py.
provenance_note: Written after E33 was read and after ONE tiny smoke run (seed 0, 16 chains, gap8 only, grid 201, --quick) had been looked at: its hidden-site errors were within 1% across all arms and the linear interval was wider (2.76 against 2.30). P4 was ORIGINALLY 'linear error >= 1.3 x oracle on gap16'; that glimpse made it implausible, so P4 and P5 were rewritten to what is actually expected (the benefit is the uncertainty, not the mean) before the full run. P1-P3 were written before that glimpse and are unchanged.
resources: laptop, one core per cell; about 15 minutes in all (BP and FFBS only, no EM)
status: REGISTERED and PREDECLARED 2026-10-08, before the confirmatory run; RUN and FROZEN 2026-10-08 (laptop, 480 rows, commit 34e8d3a, clean) and READ: P1, P2, P4 CONFIRMED; P3 and P5 FALSIFIED, both narrowly

outcome.read: 2026-10-08 ~00:40 CEST, outputs/E45/inpainting.csv (32 cells x 3 patterns x 5 arms, no failed rebuild), tools/make_extension_numbers.py as pinned before the run.
outcome.P1: CONFIRMED. The oracle's 90% intervals cover the truth with frequency 0.890-0.893 on every (cell, pattern), pooled over seeds (per-seed range 0.873-0.911).
outcome.P2: CONFIRMED. The learned site energy covers 0.890-0.893 on all six (cell, pattern) and its hidden-site error is within 10% of the oracle's in 16 of 16 seeds on all six; the ratio to the oracle's error is 1.000 and the interval width ratio 1.00 (to three digits). The learned tilted spline is the same.
outcome.P3: FALSIFIED, narrowly, and in the other direction from the mechanism I had in mind. The linear conditional's coverage on (T0.3_h1_L32, gap16) is 0.926, a deviation of +0.026 from 0.90 (threshold 0.03): it OVER-covers, because its intervals are wider, not because they are miscalibrated downwards.
outcome.P4: CONFIRMED. On (T0.3_h1_L32, gap16) the linear / oracle hidden-site error is 1.015.
outcome.P5: FALSIFIED, narrowly. The linear 90% interval is 1.094 times as wide as the oracle's on (T0.3_h1_L32, gap16) (threshold 1.10).
outcome.unregistered: The nonlinear posterior is close to the Gaussian one here. Hidden-site error against the oracle, base cell: linear 1.015 (gap16), 1.028 (gap8), 1.046 (random half); mixture 1.016, 1.029, 1.047 (it sits on the linear floor, as in E33); site energy and spline 1.000. T = 1 cell: every arm within 0.9% of the oracle, interval width within 2.1%. Coverage of the learned and oracle intervals is 0.89 everywhere (not 0.90): the FFBS grid and the 200-sample quantiles cost about 0.01. At t = 0.5 and these patterns the benefit of the exact nonlinear posterior over a Gaussian smoother is small (at most 4.6% in error, 9% in interval width, on the base cell); what the experiment establishes is that the fitted kernels lose nothing to the oracle, so the machinery (BP, FFBS, the learned kernel) is sound for missing data. A noise level lower than 0.5 or longer gaps would be the place to look for a larger gap; not run.
